## Authority and permits

**Profile in use: Unincorporated Williamson County, Texas** (`unincorporated_wilco`; the other profile: Inside a Williamson County city (`city`)).

Outside city limits the Williamson County Fire Marshal is the fire code official: 2018 International Fire Code with county amendments (the Williamson County Fire Code, effective November 2020). Permits and inspections are requested through wilcopermits.com. The county's published permit list has no building or electrical permit, so building and electrical work rely on the engineer of record, TDLR-licensed electricians, and third-party testing (inferred from the published list; confirm with the county).

| Permit | Issued by | When | Inspections |
|---|---|---|---|
| AHJ-FM-CON Fire Marshal construction permit | Williamson County Fire Marshal | Before construction that changes the building or its fire protection; plans for projects of 5,000 sq ft or more are signed and sealed by a Texas architect or engineer. | Non-structural architectural and fire protection plan review; Final inspection |
| AHJ-FM-FA Fire alarm permit | Williamson County Fire Marshal | When detection or notification is added or changed (for example VESDA sampling or new detectors). Plans sealed by a fire protection engineer or signed by a licensed APS, with battery and voltage calculations. | Fire alarm acceptance test on normal and battery power |
| AHJ-FM-SPK Fire sprinkler permit | Williamson County Fire Marshal | When sprinkler piping or heads change (for example relocating heads around new rack rows). Hydraulic calculations and a product submittal. | Hydrostatic test and flush; Flow and tamper switch test; Final inspection |
| AHJ-FM-COC Certificate of Compliance | Williamson County Fire Marshal | Issued by the Fire Marshal after the final inspections pass. | - |

| Hall at design | UPS, normal (busiest module) | 1,056 kW | 1,500 kW | 70% | 80% | Pass | 4 x 1,500 kW sharing 4,224 kW |
| Hall at design | UPS, one module lost (4 make 3) | 1,452 kW | 1,500 kW | 97% | 100% | Pass | lost module's groups shift to their other feed |
| Hall at design | Unit substation (worst UPS input) | 1,663 kVA | 2,500 kVA | 67% | 100% | Pass | UPS input at worst case plus battery recharge |
| Hall at design | Busway, one feed lost (largest segment) | 962 A | 1,200 A | 80% | 90% | Pass | 6 racks x 132 kW on one 1200 A busway |
| Hall at design | Mechanical UPS (2N, one unit carries all) | 129 kW | 300 kW | 43% | 100% | Pass | CDU pumps and thermal-wall fans |

| Hall at design | Electrical room CRAH, N+1 | 131 kW | 200 kW | 65% | 100% | Pass | power conversion losses |

| Hall at reported peak | UPS, one module lost (4 make 3) | 1,705 kW | 1,500 kW | 114% | 100% | **Control:** Rack power limit set at or below 132 kW before energization (M4) | lost module's groups shift to their other feed |
| Hall at reported peak | Unit substation (worst UPS input) | 1,953 kVA | 2,500 kVA | 78% | 100% | Pass | UPS input at worst case plus battery recharge |

| Per rack | Tap-off breaker, one feed carries the rack (design) | 225 A | 225 A | 100% | 100% | Pass | 132 kW at 480 V, PF 0.99: 160 A continuous; x 1.25 = 200 A, next standard size 225 A against the 225 A tap-off |
| Per rack | Tap-off breaker, one feed carries the rack (reported peak) | 250 A | 225 A | 111% | 100% | **Control:** Rack power limit set at or below 132 kW before energization (M4) | 155 kW at 480 V, PF 0.99: 188 A continuous; x 1.25 = 235 A, next standard size 250 A against the 225 A tap-off |
| Per rack | Floor load under the rack footprint | 18.5 kPa | 24.0 kPa | 77% | 100% | Pass | 1,360 kg on 600 x 1200 mm |

| Per rack | Coolant flow | 142.6 LPM | - | - | - | Figure | 1.2 LPM per kW of liquid heat |
| Per rack | Coolant temperature rise across the rack | 12.7 K | - | - | - | Figure | Q = m x cp x dT with 1.02 kg/L and 3.85 kJ/kg K |

Calculation inputs the site model does not hold:

- `rack_peak_kw` = 155: reported peak (EDPp class) for GB300 NVL72; published range 132 to 140 kW operating
- `rack_weight_kg` = 1360: reported, about 1.36 t loaded; varies by OEM chassis
- `floor_rating_kpa` = 24.0: assumption: slab-on-grade data hall floor rated 24 kPa (about 500 psf) uniform load
- `tap_off_breaker_a` = 225: assumption: 225 A, 3-pole tap-off breaker per rack feed
- `continuous_factor` = 1.25: NEC: overcurrent device at 125% of continuous load
- `standard_breaker_a` = [100, 110, 125, 150, 175, 200, 225, 250, 300, 350, 400]: NEC 240.6(A) standard ampere ratings (excerpt)
- `coolant_density_kg_per_l` = 1.02: assumption: 25% propylene glycol secondary coolant
- `coolant_cp_kj_per_kg_k` = 3.85: assumption: 25% propylene glycol secondary coolant

## Steps

### G0 Design and approvals

#### G0-01 Owner's project requirements and basis of design

- **Document:** DEP-B-OPR-01 (Requirements)
- **Performed by:** Customer Deployment Lead
- **Standards:** ASHRAE Guideline 0, The Commissioning Process

Procedure:

1. Customer writes the owner's project requirements: rack product (GB300 NVL72), count (32), power cap per rack, redundancy (2N power to the rack, N+1 CDUs), schedule, and acceptance tests.
2. Landlord's engineer of record answers with the basis of design for power, cooling, and fire protection.
3. The commissioning agent reviews both and opens the issues log.

Acceptance:

- Every requirement has a design answer or an open issue with an owner.

Records: Owner's project requirements (signed); Basis of design (signed); Commissioning issues log.

Sign-off, in order: Customer Deployment Lead -> Landlord engineer of record (Texas PE) -> Commissioning agent (Customer-engaged).

#### G0-02 Load calculations: power, cooling, floor, cabling

- **Document:** DEP-B-CALC-01 (Calculation sheet)
- **Performed by:** Landlord engineer of record (Texas PE)
- **After:** G0-01
- **Standards:** NFPA 70, National Electrical Code (2026 in Texas from 2026-09-01)

Procedure:

1. Run the calculation sheet on this tab against the site model: UPS, unit substation, busway, tap-off, CDU heat and flow, thermal walls, floor load, cable counts.
2. Repeat the power checks at the rack's reported peak, not only at the design figure.
3. Every check that fails at peak becomes a required control (for example the rack power cap) carried into the rack milestones.

Acceptance:

- Every design check passes, and every peak check passes or has a named control.

Records: Calculation sheet (sealed); Controls list.

Sign-off, in order: Landlord engineer of record (Texas PE) -> Customer Facilities Engineer -> IT Partner deployment lead.

#### G0-03 Construction documents sealed

- **Document:** DEP-B-CD-01 (Drawing set)
- **Performed by:** Landlord engineer of record (Texas PE)
- **After:** G0-02
- **Standards:** NFPA 70, National Electrical Code (2026 in Texas from 2026-09-01); 2018 International Fire Code with Williamson County amendments; ANSI/TIA-942-C (2024)

Procedure:

1. Issue the drawing set: one-lines, busway and tap-off schedule, piping and valve schedule, fire protection changes, cable pathways and labeling.
2. Seal the set (Texas PE); the Customer and the IT Partner review the rack interface sheets.

Acceptance:

- Set sealed; review comments closed.

Records: Sealed drawing set; Review comment log.

Sign-off, in order: Landlord engineer of record (Texas PE) -> Customer Facilities Engineer -> IT Partner deployment lead.

#### G0-04 Permits and determinations

- **Document:** DEP-B-PRM-01 (Permit register)
- **Performed by:** Landlord engineer of record (Texas PE)
- **After:** G0-03
- **Standards:** 2018 International Fire Code with Williamson County amendments; NFPA 70, National Electrical Code (2026 in Texas from 2026-09-01)

Procedure:

1. List every permit the authority profile requires for this scope and apply for each.
2. Record the statewide determinations: accessibility (TDLR registration or not covered), large-load interconnection (site peak against the threshold), and which NEC edition applies by permit date.
3. Post permits on site; schedule required inspections into the step that triggers them.

Acceptance:

- Every required permit issued; every determination recorded with its reason.

Records: Permit register; Determinations.

Sign-off, in order: Landlord engineer of record (Texas PE) -> Customer Deployment Lead.

Inspections:

- Authority: Williamson County Fire Marshal, Plan review (construction, fire alarm, sprinkler as applicable)

#### G0-05 Change approval and Landlord MOPs

- **Document:** DEP-B-CHG-01 (Change record)
- **Performed by:** Customer change board
- **After:** G0-03

Procedure:

1. Customer change board approves the program change and the method statements of each partner.
2. The Landlord submits a MOP for each energization (Interface Agreement HO-4) for Customer approval before its window.

Acceptance:

- Program change approved; MOP template for tap-off energization approved.

Records: Change record; Approved MOP template.

Sign-off, in order: Customer change board -> Landlord facility operations -> IT Partner deployment lead.

#### G0-06 Delivery schedule and receiving plan

- **Document:** DEP-B-SCH-01 (Schedule)
- **Performed by:** IT Partner deployment lead
- **After:** G0-01

Procedure:

1. Commit a planned receipt date and a handoff date for every rack (the rack cycle target is in the IT Partner SLA).
2. Plan the receiving route: dock, route survey, floor-load check, rated powered equipment, spotter.

Acceptance:

- Every rack has a committed handoff date; route survey signed.

Records: Deployment plan; Route survey.

Sign-off, in order: IT Partner deployment lead -> Customer Deployment Lead -> Landlord facility operations.

#### G0-07 Site safety plan

- **Document:** DEP-B-EHS-01 (Safety plan)
- **Performed by:** IT Partner deployment lead
- **After:** G0-01
- **Standards:** NFPA 70E, Electrical Safety in the Workplace (current edition); OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147; OSHA 29 CFR 1926

Procedure:

1. Each partner submits its site-specific safety plan: energized work policy, lockout/tagout, rigging and rack moves, coolant spill response, hot work.
2. Agree whose lock goes on which device at the interface (Landlord on the tap-off, IT Partner on the rack).

Acceptance:

- Both plans accepted by the Customer; interface lockout points agreed.

Records: Safety plans; Lockout point list.

Sign-off, in order: IT Partner deployment lead -> Landlord facility operations -> Customer Deployment Lead.

### G1 Hall readiness

#### G1-01 Receipt inspection: busway, tap-offs, CDUs (L2)

- **Document:** DEP-B-CX-L2-01 (Checklist)
- **Performed by:** Landlord quality control
- **Commissioning level:** L2
- **After:** G0-04
- **Standards:** Commissioning levels L1 to L5

Procedure:

1. Inspect each delivery against the submittal: model, rating, quantity, damage, factory test reports (L1) on file.
2. Tag the equipment yellow when accepted.

Acceptance:

- Every item matches its submittal with its factory test report.

Records: Receipt checklists; Factory test reports.

Sign-off, in order: Landlord quality control -> Commissioning agent (Customer-engaged).

#### G1-02 Busway and tap-off installation and testing (L3)

- **Document:** DEP-B-CX-L3-01 (Test script)
- **Performed by:** Landlord electrical contractor (TDLR-licensed)
- **Commissioning level:** L3
- **After:** G1-01
- **Standards:** ANSI/NETA ATS-2025; NFPA 70, National Electrical Code (2026 in Texas from 2026-09-01); NFPA 70E, Electrical Safety in the Workplace (current edition)

Procedure:

1. Install the A and B busway runs and the tap-offs to the sealed schedule; torque every joint to the manufacturer's value and mark it.
2. Acceptance-test to ANSI/NETA ATS: visual and mechanical inspection, insulation resistance, joint resistance, breaker tests.
3. Apply arc flash labels from the study; verify each tap-off's label and rack position.

Acceptance:

- Every test result within ATS limits; every torque mark present; labels match the schedule.

Records: NETA test reports; Torque log; Arc flash labels.

Sign-off, in order: Landlord electrical contractor (TDLR-licensed) -> Landlord quality control -> Electrical testing firm (NETA-accredited) -> Commissioning agent (Customer-engaged).

Inspections:

- Third party: Electrical testing firm (NETA-accredited), Acceptance test of busway and tap-offs

#### G1-03 Secondary loop pressure test, flush, and fill (L3)

- **Document:** DEP-B-CX-L3-02 (Test script)
- **Performed by:** Landlord facility operations
- **Commissioning level:** L3
- **After:** G1-01

Procedure:

1. Hydrostatically test the Hall B secondary header and row manifolds at the specified test pressure; hold and record.
2. Flush through temporary strainers until clean to the CDU vendor's cleanliness specification; remove strainers.
3. Fill with the specified coolant, vent, and sample it for the laboratory.

Acceptance:

- Pressure held with no decay over the hold period; flush samples clean; laboratory results within the fluid specification.

Records: Pressure test chart; Flush log; Coolant laboratory report.

Sign-off, in order: Landlord facility operations -> Landlord quality control -> Coolant test laboratory -> Commissioning agent (Customer-engaged).

Inspections:

- Internal: Customer witness, Witness the pressure test
- Third party: Coolant test laboratory, Coolant analysis

#### G1-04 CDU start-up (L3) and functional test (L4)

- **Document:** DEP-B-CX-L4-01 (Test script)
- **Performed by:** OEM field service
- **Commissioning level:** L4
- **After:** G1-03, G1-02
- **Standards:** Commissioning levels L1 to L5

Procedure:

1. OEM starts each CDU-B1 to B4: pump rotation, sensors, controls, alarms to the BMS.
2. Functional test: lead pump fail to lag; one CDU off with the other three carrying design flow (N+1); loss of facility water alarm; leak and low-level alarms.

Acceptance:

- Every sequence behaves as written; supply temperature and flow hold during each failover.

Records: Start-up reports; L4 functional test results.

Sign-off, in order: OEM field service -> Landlord facility operations -> Commissioning agent (Customer-engaged) -> Customer witness.

#### G1-05 Fire and life safety changes (L4)

- **Document:** DEP-B-CX-L4-02 (Test script)
- **Performed by:** Landlord facility operations
- **Commissioning level:** L4
- **After:** G1-01
- **When:** When the rack layout changes detection, sprinklers, or notification.
- **Standards:** 2018 International Fire Code with Williamson County amendments

Procedure:

1. Test the VESDA sampling network (transport time to each end hole) and the leak detection circuits under the new rows.
2. Run the fire alarm acceptance test on normal and battery power; schedule the authority's finals.

Acceptance:

- Transport times within the design; every leak circuit alarms at the BMS and the Customer's collector; finals passed.

Records: VESDA commissioning report; Fire alarm test report; Final inspection results.

Sign-off, in order: Landlord facility operations -> Commissioning agent (Customer-engaged) -> Customer witness.

Inspections:

- Authority: Williamson County Fire Marshal, Fire alarm and sprinkler finals

#### G1-06 Monitoring point-to-point (L4)

- **Document:** DEP-B-CX-L4-03 (Points list)
- **Performed by:** Landlord facility operations
- **Commissioning level:** L4
- **After:** G1-02, G1-04

Procedure:

1. Prove every Hall B point end to end: busway and tap-off meters, CDU, leak, VESDA, to the BMS and to the Customer's Telemetry of Record collector.
2. Force each alarm at the device and record the time it appears in both systems.

Acceptance:

- Every point reads the same value in both systems; every alarm arrives at both.

Records: Points list with results.

Sign-off, in order: Landlord facility operations -> Commissioning agent (Customer-engaged) -> Customer Facilities Engineer.

#### G1-07 Integrated systems test (L5)

- **Document:** DEP-B-CX-L5-01 (Test script)
- **Performed by:** Commissioning agent (Customer-engaged)
- **Commissioning level:** L5
- **After:** G1-04, G1-05, G1-06
- **Standards:** Commissioning levels L1 to L5; NFPA 70E, Electrical Safety in the Workplace (current edition)

Procedure:

1. Load Hall B with load banks at the design kW per rack position (liquid load banks on the manifolds, air load banks for the air share).
2. Open the utility feed: UPSs carry the load on battery, generators start and take the load, CDU pumps stay on the mechanical UPS, flow never stops.
3. Fail one UPS module (4 make 3) and one CDU (N+1) under load; restore utility and return to normal.

Acceptance:

- No loss of power at any rack position; coolant flow and supply temperature within limits through every transfer; every alarm as expected.

Records: L5 test report with trend data; Issues log closed or accepted.

Sign-off, in order: Commissioning agent (Customer-engaged) -> Landlord facility operations -> Landlord engineer of record (Texas PE) -> Customer witness -> Customer Deployment Lead.

Inspections:

- Internal: Customer witness, Witness the full test

#### G1-08 Ready for racks

- **Document:** DEP-B-RFR-01 (Certificate)
- **Performed by:** Landlord facility operations
- **After:** G1-07

Procedure:

1. Landlord declares Hall B ready for racks: open issues listed with dates, access control and CCTV working, spares stocked, hall clean.

Acceptance:

- Customer accepts the certificate and its open-issues list.

Records: Ready-for-racks certificate.

Sign-off, in order: Landlord facility operations -> Commissioning agent (Customer-engaged) -> Customer security and asset management -> Customer Deployment Lead.

### G2 Rack waves

#### R-M1 Received and inspected

- **Document:** DEP-B-RK-01 (Checklist)
- **Performed by:** IT Partner deployment lead
- **Rack milestone:** M1, target day 1 from receipt (IT Partner SLA)
- **After:** G1-08

Procedure:

1. Receive the rack at the dock; check shock and tilt indicators before unwrapping; photograph.
2. Reconcile serials and asset tags to the advance shipping notice; record any damage with the carrier.
3. Move to position on rated powered equipment along the surveyed route, with a spotter.

Acceptance:

- Shock and tilt indicators checked; no shipping damage; asset tags and serials reconciled to the ASN.

Records: Receiving checklist; Photos; Serial reconciliation.

Sign-off, in order: IT Partner deployment lead -> IT Partner quality control -> Customer security and asset management.

#### R-M2 Positioned and connected

- **Document:** DEP-B-RK-02 (Checklist)
- **Performed by:** IT Partner deployment lead
- **Rack milestone:** M2, target day 3 from receipt (IT Partner SLA)
- **After:** R-M1

Procedure:

1. Set and secure the rack; level it; fit seismic or anti-tip bracing if specified.
2. Connect the supply and return hoses at the rack isolation valves (valves stay closed); connect the A and B power cords to the de-energized tap-offs.
3. Confirm the tap-off labels match the rack and the schedule.

Acceptance:

- Rack set and secured; power whips and manifold connected at the rack isolation valves.

Records: Set and connect checklist.

Sign-off, in order: IT Partner deployment lead -> IT Partner quality control.

#### R-M3 Leak test passed

- **Document:** DEP-B-RK-03 (Test record)
- **Performed by:** IT Partner deployment lead
- **Rack milestone:** M3, target day 4 from receipt (IT Partner SLA)
- **After:** R-M2

Procedure:

1. Pressure-test the rack's liquid path at the OEM test pressure with the isolation valves closed; hold and record.
2. Confirm zero leak alarms at the row's leak circuit.

Acceptance:

- Pressure hold at the OEM test pressure (typically 1.5x operating) for at least 30 minutes with no decay; zero leak alarms; coolant within specification.

Records: Pressure test record.

Sign-off, in order: IT Partner deployment lead -> IT Partner quality control -> Customer witness.

#### R-HO4 Energize tap-offs and open isolation valves (Interface Agreement HO-4)

- **Document:** DEP-B-RK-HO4 (MOP)
- **Performed by:** Landlord facility operations
- **After:** R-M3
- **Standards:** NFPA 70E, Electrical Safety in the Workplace (current edition); OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147

Procedure:

1. IT Partner confirms in writing that the rack is set, leak-tested, and ready (M3 signed).
2. Landlord runs its approved MOP: remove its locks, close the A and B tap-off breakers, open the supply and return isolation valves slowly, watch for leaks.
3. Record the handoff time; it is the deployment milestone handoff in the Interface Agreement.

Acceptance:

- Both feeds live at the rack; flow established; no leak alarm.

Records: Approved MOP; Energization record.

Sign-off, in order: Landlord facility operations -> IT Partner deployment lead.

#### R-M4 Power-on and firmware baseline

- **Document:** DEP-B-RK-04 (Checklist)
- **Performed by:** IT Partner deployment lead
- **Rack milestone:** M4, target day 5 from receipt (IT Partner SLA)
- **After:** R-HO4

Procedure:

1. Power on; confirm POST on every tray and BMC reachable on the out-of-band network.
2. Load the Customer's firmware baseline; set and verify the rack power limit (the control from the calculation sheet) before any load.

Acceptance:

- POST clean on all trays; firmware matches the Customer baseline; BMCs reachable on OOB.

Records: Firmware report; Power limit setting.

Sign-off, in order: IT Partner deployment lead -> IT Partner quality control.

#### R-M5 Network cabled and verified

- **Document:** DEP-B-RK-05 (Test record)
- **Performed by:** IT Partner deployment lead
- **Rack milestone:** M5, target day 7 from receipt (IT Partner SLA)
- **After:** R-M4
- **Standards:** ANSI/TIA-942-C (2024)

Procedure:

1. Cable every back-end link to its leaf port per the cabling plan (one NIC per rail per tray); label both ends.
2. Verify each link is up at full speed, error-free over the soak, and lands on the planned port.

Acceptance:

- Every back-end and front-end link up, error-free over soak, and matching the cabling plan.

Records: Cable test results; Port map check.

Sign-off, in order: IT Partner deployment lead -> IT Partner quality control.

#### R-M6 Burn-in accepted

- **Document:** DEP-B-RK-06 (Test record)
- **Performed by:** IT Partner deployment lead
- **Rack milestone:** M6, target day 9 from receipt (IT Partner SLA)
- **After:** R-M5

Procedure:

1. Run GPU diagnostics, NVLink domain acceptance, NCCL benchmarks, and the 24-hour burn-in.
2. The Customer's health checks record the burn-in result independently.

Acceptance:

- GPU diagnostics, NVLink domain acceptance, NCCL benchmarks, and 24-hour burn-in all pass.

Records: Diagnostics; Benchmark results; Burn-in result.

Sign-off, in order: IT Partner deployment lead -> IT Partner quality control -> Customer witness.

#### R-M7 Validated Handoff

- **Document:** DEP-B-RK-07 (Acceptance record)
- **Performed by:** IT Partner deployment lead
- **Rack milestone:** M7, target day 10 from receipt (IT Partner SLA)
- **After:** R-M6

Procedure:

1. Assemble the acceptance record (every record above) and release the rack to the Customer scheduler.

Acceptance:

- Rack released to the Customer scheduler with the full acceptance record. CSL-09 is measured at this milestone.

Records: Acceptance record.

Sign-off, in order: IT Partner deployment lead -> IT Partner quality control -> Customer Deployment Lead.

### G3 Closeout

#### G3-01 As-built drawings and site model updated

- **Document:** DEP-B-AB-01 (Drawing set)
- **Performed by:** Landlord engineer of record (Texas PE)
- **After:** R-M7

Procedure:

1. Fold every field change into the drawings and site/site.yaml; regenerate the drawings and the device directory.

Acceptance:


Records: As-built set.

Sign-off, in order: Landlord engineer of record (Texas PE) -> IT Partner deployment lead -> Customer Facilities Engineer.

#### G3-02 Turnover package

- **Document:** DEP-B-TO-01 (Package)
- **Performed by:** Landlord facility operations
- **After:** R-M7

Procedure:

1. Deliver O&M manuals, warranties, spare parts lists, training records, and the final commissioning report.

Acceptance:


Records: Turnover package; Final commissioning report.

Sign-off, in order: Landlord facility operations -> IT Partner deployment lead -> Commissioning agent (Customer-engaged) -> Customer Deployment Lead.

#### G3-03 Authority close-out

- **Document:** DEP-B-PRM-02 (Permit register)
- **Performed by:** Landlord engineer of record (Texas PE)
- **After:** R-M7

Procedure:

1. File the certificate (Certificate of Compliance or certificate of occupancy) and close every permit; complete the accessibility inspection if the project was determined covered.

Acceptance:


Records: Certificate; Closed permit register.

Sign-off, in order: Landlord engineer of record (Texas PE) -> Customer Deployment Lead.

Inspections:

- Authority: Registered Accessibility Specialist (TDLR), Accessibility inspection, if determined covered

#### G3-04 Lessons learned

- **Document:** DEP-B-LL-01 (Review)
- **Performed by:** Customer Deployment Lead
- **After:** G3-01, G3-02, G3-03

Procedure:

1. Review the program with both partners: what slipped, why, and which standard work changes; raise a post-incident review for any event.

Acceptance:


Records: Lessons learned.

Sign-off, in order: Customer Deployment Lead -> Landlord facility operations -> IT Partner deployment lead.

## Sign-off roles

| Role | Organization | Duty |
|---|---|---|
| Customer Deployment Lead | Customer | Owns the program; signs every gate. |
| Customer Facilities Engineer | Customer | Reviews the Landlord's design and test results for the Customer. |
| Customer witness | Customer | Witnesses tests in person and signs what was observed. |
| Customer change board | Customer | Approves changes and Landlord MOPs that touch the hall. |
| Customer security and asset management | Customer | Access lists, asset records, and chain of custody. |
| Landlord engineer of record (Texas PE) | Landlord | Seals the construction documents and the load calculations. |
| Landlord facility operations | Landlord | Operates power and cooling; performs switching and valve operations. |
| Landlord quality control | Landlord | Checks the Landlord's and its contractors' work before it is offered for test. |
| Landlord electrical contractor (TDLR-licensed) | Landlord | Installs and terminates electrical work under a licensed master electrician. |
| IT Partner deployment lead | IT Partner | Runs the rack waves; owns milestones M1 to M7. |
| IT Partner quality control | IT Partner | Checks every rack milestone against its exit criteria before it is reported. |
| Commissioning agent (Customer-engaged) | Third party | Independent: writes and runs the L3 to L5 scripts, keeps the issues log, signs the commissioning report. |
| Electrical testing firm (NETA-accredited) | Third party | Acceptance tests electrical equipment to ANSI/NETA ATS. |
| OEM field service | Third party | Factory start-up of CDUs and rack integration support. |
| Coolant test laboratory | Third party | Analyses coolant samples against the CDU vendor's fluid specification. |
| Williamson County Fire Marshal | Authority | Fire code permits, plan review, and final inspections in unincorporated Williamson County. |
| City building inspections | Authority | Building, electrical, and mechanical permits and inspections inside city limits. |
| Registered Accessibility Specialist (TDLR) | Authority | Texas Accessibility Standards review and inspection where the project is covered. |
| Serving utility (transmission service provider) | Authority | Large-load interconnection under PUCT rules. |
